storyboard.ears: A third of America now wears ink, and most can't stop at one.
In 2006, just 16 percent of Americans had a tattoo. Today that has doubled, to roughly one in three.
storyboard.eyes: substance: black tattoo ink; cause: Data shoves a giant buzzing tattoo machine down the arm and its needle inks the skin as it goes
storyboard.evidence: Pew Research Center / Ipsos / Harris Poll | Share of US adults with at least one tattoo | https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2023/08/15/32-of-americans-have-a-tattoo-including-22-who-have-more-than-one/ | 2026-09-13

storyboard.ears: Women lead the pack: 37 percent have a tattoo, against about a third of all adults. Not a rebel look anymore.
storyboard.evidence: Pew Research Center | Share with at least one tattoo, by gender | https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2023/08/15/32-of-americans-have-a-tattoo-including-22-who-have-more-than-one/ | 2026-09-13

storyboard.ears: Once people start, they rarely stop. One in five Americans has more than one tattoo, twice as many as stopped at one.
storyboard.evidence: Pew Research Center | US adults, by number of tattoos | https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2023/08/15/32-of-americans-have-a-tattoo-including-22-who-have-more-than-one/ | 2026-09-13

storyboard.ears: Tattoos stopped being rebellion once a third of America had one. That's just normal now.
